subtitle: Two ways to prove who's calling, side by side

code:
Basic:
Authorization: Basic aW50ZWdyYXRpb24udXNlcjpwYXNz

OAuth 2.0 / Bearer token:
Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6...
caption: Both ride in the same header; what's encoded after "Basic" or "Bearer" is what differs.

steps.label: Basic Auth
steps.sub: username:password, base64-encoded — same string, every call

steps.label: OAuth 2.0
steps.sub: exchange credentials once for a token that expires on its own

steps.label: Base64 ≠ encryption
steps.sub: base64 is reversible encoding, not protection by itself

steps.label: Revocation
steps.sub: a leaked token can be revoked without changing a password

steps.label: Expiration
steps.sub: a token naturally stops working; a leaked password doesn't

steps.label: MFA conflict
steps.sub: Basic Auth can't be used by users set up with MFA
